author: agent
text:
DEFECT, measured 2026-08-16: this uses builtin hash() on token tuples, which Python randomizes per process (PYTHONHASHSEED). Sketches are PERSISTED in coordinates.json and parse_cache.json, so values computed by different processes coexist and are compared to each other.

Two consequences, both reproduced. (1) Indexing the same tree in two fresh clones produces byte-identical output EXCEPT `sketch`, which differs on 888/888 entities - so `git diff --exit-code .coord` can never be a CI staleness gate, and every parallel index conflicts in coordinates.json. (2) sketch_jaccard is the largest single term in lineage's rename score (weight 0.30) and sketch_containment is the ONLY signal behind split/merge detection; across process boundaries - i.e. every real rename, since the old sketch comes off disk and the new one is computed now - both are noise. Isolated experiment, identical repo and commits, only PYTHONHASHSEED varied: default gave `lineage: deleted m.compute_totals` (no relationship recorded, attached knowledge orphaned with no trail); PYTHONHASHSEED=7 on both runs gave `merged -> m.ledger_rollup - needs confirmation` (recorded, pending-review, recoverable). Randomization converts "flagged for a human" into "silently deleted".

Fix is a stable hash (e.g. blake2b of the joined tokens), but note the migration: existing persisted sketches are random values, so the change must bump the parse schema version and force a full recompute in ONE pass, or old-vs-new comparisons will read as zero similarity for exactly one transition - the same failure this note describes.
